common_issues: Oil weights across all five oils (mustard, sunflower, groundnut, coconut, sesame) are computed correctly at density ~0.91 g/ml — tbsp 14g, tsp 4.5g, katori 135g all check out. Excellent consistency.

Allergen tagging is correct across the batch: mustard→mustard, groundnut→peanuts, sesame→sesame, egg→eggs, prawns→shellfish, fish entries→fish, sunflower and coconut oils correctly empty (coconut isn't classified as tree nut under Indian/EU/FSSAI conventions; the controlled vocab decision to leave empty is correct).

canonical_form continues the pattern of full descriptive phrases ('raw boneless chicken breast', 'whole chicken egg', 'mustard oil') rather than the {raw, cooked} controlled vocab. Same global concern as previous batches — needs a normalisation pass.

Meat/fish/seafood piece weights are mostly reasonable but two domain-specific issues worth attention: 'mutton' (means goat in Indian context, not sheep — affects nutrition lookup ~2.7x) and pomfret piece weight is on the small side relative to typical market sizing.

issues.problem: 'raw boneless chicken breast' should normalise to 'raw'. The 'boneless' qualifier is meaningful and can move to typical_form_note.
issues.suggested_fix: canonical_form='raw'; update typical_form_note to clarify 'boneless, measured raw before cooking'.

issues.problem: 'raw chicken thigh' should normalise to 'raw'. Note that bone-in vs boneless matters nutritionally (calories per 'piece' include or exclude bone weight) — currently 'piece' notes say 'bone-in' which is consistent with Indian curry-cut convention.

'Mutton' in Indian English universally means goat meat (chevon), NOT sheep. But the same word in UK/US/Australian usage means mature sheep meat. The two have very different macronutrient profiles: goat is lean (~109 kcal/100g raw, ~20g protein, ~2g fat) while sheep mutton is fatty (~294 kcal/100g raw, ~25g protein, ~21g fat). If your nutrition lookup hits a USDA-style 'mutton' reference, every Indian mutton recipe will over-count calories by ~2.7x.
issues.suggested_fix: Either: (a) rename to 'mutton (goat)' or 'goat meat' to make the species explicit; (b) keep name 'mutton' but ensure your nutrition lookup is pinned to a goat (chevon) reference, not a sheep reference. Strongly recommend (a) for ambiguity safety, especially if you ever ingest international recipe data.

issues.problem: 'whole chicken egg' has no form token. Eggs are nearly always cooked before eating but measured raw. 'raw' is the right token.
issues.suggested_fix: canonical_form='raw'. typical_form_note already says 'measured whole with shell removed' which is accurate.

issues.problem: 1 medium whole pomfret cleaned = 180g is on the small side. Indian silver/black pomfret market sizing: small 150-200g whole-cleaned, medium 250-350g, large 400g+. 180g is closer to a small fish.
issues.suggested_fix: Either change to approximate_grams=280 (mid-medium) or update notes to 'small whole pomfret, cleaned'. The current value is defensible for small fish but mislabeled as 'medium'.

issues.problem: 'mustard oil' has no form token. Oils are 'raw' in the sense of being unmodified at point of use.
